questions.q: What two requirements must an Apex method meet before an LWC component can call it at all?
options: It must be public (or global) and static, and annotated @AuraEnabled
It must be private and non-static
It must return a String and take no parameters
It must be declared inside a Visualforce controller extension
questions.explain: An Apex method callable from LWC must be public or global, static, and annotated with @AuraEnabled -- without all of these, the method is not exposed to the client at all.

questions.q: What is the correct import syntax for an Apex method named `getAccounts` on an Apex class named `AccountController`?
options: import { getAccounts } from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController';
import AccountController from '@salesforce/apex/getAccounts';
import getAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccounts';
import getAccounts from 'apex/AccountController/getAccounts';
questions.explain: The import path always follows @salesforce/apex/ClassName.methodName, and since the method itself is the module's default export, it's imported with no curly braces: `import getAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccounts';`.

questions.q: Why can't an Apex method that performs DML ever be used with the @wire decorator?
options: @wire only supports methods that return primitive types, not sObjects
DML operations are not allowed inside any @AuraEnabled method
@wire requires the method to be @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true), and a method with DML or other side effects cannot be marked cacheable=true
@wire can only call methods with zero parameters
questions.explain: cacheable=true declares a method read-only and safe to cache -- a requirement for @wire. A method performing DML has side effects, so it cannot be cacheable=true, and therefore cannot be wired; it must be called imperatively instead.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which scenario calls for an imperative Apex call rather than a wired one?
options: Loading read-only data as soon as the component first renders
Imperative calls are never appropriate in LWC
Any method that is annotated cacheable=true
A write operation, or data that needs to be fetched in response to a specific user action like a button click
questions.explain: Imperative calls fit situations where the call should happen in response to something specific -- a button click, a search as the user types, or any write operation -- rather than automatically on load.

questions.q: In an imperative Apex call wrapped in try/catch, where does the error's human-readable message typically live?
options: error.message, exactly like a plain JavaScript Error
error.detail.reason
error.body.message
Apex errors never surface a readable message to JavaScript
questions.explain: An Apex call's rejected error object typically carries its human-readable message at error.body.message, which is why error handling code commonly reads from that path rather than error.message directly.
